Why this matters

Traditional aid reporting can be delayed and difficult to audit. AidChain makes each funding action traceable and ties fund release to reviewed milestones.

Privacy by design: personal beneficiary details stay off the public ledger.

Milestone status

Role-based workflow

Switch the demo role at the top right to test NGO submissions and reviewer approvals.

NGO Project Manager: submit an evidence reference for a milestone.

Community Reviewer: approve or reject a submitted milestone. Approval triggers a simulated release from available project funds.

Donor / Public: inspect progress and audit entries without approval privileges.

Production would require wallet signatures, independent reviewers, dispute handling, and smart contract enforcement.

Funding and outcomes by project

Measurement framework

Inputs: contributions committed to a named project. Outputs: approved milestones and released funding. Outcomes: independent verification of actual community benefits (future production integration). Safeguards: minimal beneficiary data, consent, and accessible public reporting.

Judge-ready demonstration · 5-minute script

1. Open Projects & Donations and inspect a project. 2. Select 100 demo USDC, review the contribution, and enter a fictional DEMO- reference. 3. Save the simulated receipt. 4. Switch to NGO Project Manager, create a community project and submit milestone evidence. 5. Switch to Community Reviewer to approve evidence, then demonstrate a simulated release. 6. Verify and export the local audit ledger.

All actions are local simulations. The browser hash chain is illustrative and is not immutable, on-chain, or proof of an actual donation.

From vision to impact

A transparent funding workflow designed for communities, NGOs, and donors.

How the demo works

1. A project sets a funding goal and milestones.

2. Donors contribute simulated USDC.

3. NGO managers submit milestone evidence references.

4. Reviewers approve or reject submissions.

5. Approved milestones release available funds and create audit records.

6. Anyone can inspect activity and outcomes.

Planned Web3 production layer

Escrow smart contracts, verified project registry, signed donor transactions, multisignature reviewer authorization, milestone-specific payouts, event indexing, and content-addressed evidence stored off-chain.

Why Web3? To reduce unilateral control of escrow balances and provide independently verifiable payment and approval history.

What is not built here? Real blockchain settlement, verified identity, anti-fraud investigation, oracles, secure file storage, independent auditing, and production compliance.

Judge demo script (3 minutes)

0:00–0:30: Explain the aid transparency problem. 0:30–1:00: Show projects and donation progress. 1:00–1:40: Donate simulated USDC and show the audit entry. 1:40–2:20: Switch to NGO role, submit evidence; switch to Reviewer, approve the milestone. 2:20–2:45: Show released funds and ledger verification. 2:45–3:00: Explain production smart contracts and measurable impact.
